sections.overview: The House Sparrow is a highly human-associated passerine now established across much of the world.
sections.identification: The male has a grey crown and black bib; the female is duller brown, with a pale eyebrow and no black bib.
sections.habitat: It commonly nests in cavities and crevices in buildings, but also uses hedges and nest boxes.
sections.diet: Adults eat seeds and scraps, while growing chicks are fed many insects.
sections.behavior: It is a sociable bird, often feeding or roosting in groups around human settlements.
sections.reproduction: It nests in cavities and can raise several broods in a long, favorable season.
sections.ecology: Compare the related Eurasian Tree Sparrow profile: that species has a chestnut crown and a black cheek spot, and the sexes look alike; the House Sparrow shows stronger sexual plumage differences.
sections.conservation: The species remains widespread globally, but it is Red-listed in the UK, reflecting regional concern.
